questions.q: Select the antonym of the word 'Fallacy'.
questions.x: 'Fallacy' is the opposite of 'Truth'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Fallacy'.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To bury the hatchet'
questions.x: 'To bury the hatchet' means: to make peace.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Nonchalant'.
questions.x: 'Nonchalant' means unconcerned. 'Anxious' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: PROFANE
questions.x: 'Profane' is the opposite of 'Sacred'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Profane'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
I look forward to / meet you / at the conference next week.
questions.x: The error is in part (b): 'meet you'. 'Look forward to' is followed by a gerund: 'meeting you'.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Reticent'.
questions.x: 'Reticent' means reserved. 'Talkative' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To have a chip on one's shoulder'
o: To be proud of an achievement
To hold a grudge or feel resentful
questions.x: 'To have a chip on one's shoulder' means: to hold a grudge or feel resentful.

questions.q: Select the synonym of the word 'Conspicuous'.
questions.x: 'Conspicuous' means noticeable. 'Hidden' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q: Neither the manager nor the clerks ____ present at the meeting.
questions.x: With 'neither…nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('clerks' — plural).

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'A person who hates mankind'
questions.x: 'Misanthrope' means a person who hates mankind.

questions.q: According to the author, what is more valuable than celebrating success?
questions.x: Answer: 'Learning from failure'. The first sentence states this. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Celebrating success is easy; learning from failure is harder and more valuable. A project that misses its target holds lessons about assumptions, timelines and coordination. Yet teams often rush to close such files quietly. A short, blame-free review that records what went wrong and what to change next time turns an expensive failure into a cheap lesson for the future.

questions.q: What does the author mean by turning 'an expensive failure into a cheap lesson'?
o: Using a review of the failure to avoid costly mistakes in future
questions.x: Answer: 'Using a review of the failure to avoid costly mistakes in future'. A blame-free review captures lessons that prevent future losses. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Celebrating success is easy; learning from failure is harder and more valuable. A project that misses its target holds lessons about assumptions, timelines and coordination. Yet teams often rush to close such files quietly. A short, blame-free review that records what went wrong and what to change next time turns an expensive failure into a cheap lesson for the future.

questions.q: Who presided over the 1889 session of the Indian National Congress held at Bombay?
questions.x: William Wedderburn presided over the 1889 Bombay session — a session presided over by a retired British civil servant.

questions.q:
In which year did the following take place?
The Congress Socialist Party was formed.
questions.x: The Congress Socialist Party was formed in 1934. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The Moderates in the early Congress relied mainly on methods of:
o: Petitions, prayers and protests within the constitutional framework
questions.x: Correct answer: Petitions, prayers and protests within the constitutional framework. Their methods are often summarised as the '3 Ps'.

questions.q: The Kakori train action (1925) was carried out by the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Hindustan Republican Association. Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan and others were later executed.

questions.q: Dadabhai Naoroji is associated with the founding of:
questions.x: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association (London, 1866).

questions.q: The book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' was written by:
questions.x: 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' was written by V. D. Savarkar.

questions.q: The committee appointed by the British government to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre was headed by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Lord Hunter. The Congress set up its own inquiry committee.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'Iron Man of India'?
questions.x: His birth anniversary (31 October) is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas.

questions.q: Who among the following founded the 'Indian Home Rule Society' in London (1905)?
questions.x: Correct answer: Shyamji Krishna Varma. He also published 'The Indian Sociologist'.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The Simon Commission was boycotted by the Congress.
Reason (R): The Commission recommended immediate independence for India.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true; R is false — the Commission was all-white and did not recommend independence.

questions.q: The 2024 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to:
questions.x: The Japanese organisation of atomic bomb survivors works for a world free of nuclear weapons. Machado won in 2025.

questions.q: National Handloom Day is observed on:
questions.x: National Handloom Day: 7 August.

questions.q: The Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (2022) includes the '30 by 30' target, which means:
o: Conserving at least 30% of land and oceans by 2030
questions.x: Correct answer: Conserving at least 30% of land and oceans by 2030. It was adopted at COP15 of the Convention on Biological Diversity.

questions.q: The G7 Summit in June 2025 was hosted by Canada at:
questions.x: Correct answer: Kananaskis. Italy hosted in 2024 (Apulia) and Japan in 2023 (Hiroshima).

questions.q: The headquarters of the Green Climate Fund is located in:
questions.x: Green Climate Fund: headquartered in Songdo (South Korea).

questions.q: NEP 2020 recommends instruction preferably in the mother tongue/local language at least up to:
questions.x: Correct answer: Class 5 (preferably Class 8). It encourages multilingualism.

questions.q:
Consider the following about the Paris 2024 Olympics:
1. India won no gold medal.
2. India's hockey team won bronze.
3. Vinesh Phogat won a silver medal in wrestling.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Vinesh Phogat was disqualified before the final for being overweight; Aman Sehrawat won bronze in wrestling.

questions.q: The military exercise 'Ekuverin' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'Ekuverin' is a bilateral exercise between India and Maldives.

questions.q: In June–July 2025, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla became:
o: The first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station (Axiom-4 mission)
The first Indian to walk on the Moon
questions.x: Correct answer: The first Indian astronaut to visit the International Space Station (Axiom-4 mission). Rakesh Sharma (1984) was the first Indian in space.

questions.q: India won the ICC Champions Trophy in March 2025 by defeating which team in the final?
questions.x: Correct answer: New Zealand. The final was held in Dubai.

questions.q: The sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court (including the CJI) after the 2019 amendment is:
questions.x: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 raised it from 31 to 34.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Composition of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 80.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Protection of monuments and places of national importance"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 49.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Money Bills can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha.
Reason (R): The Lok Sabha is directly elected and the Council of Ministers is responsible to it.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Financial control rests with the popular House, which explains the rule.

questions.q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission is chaired by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Arvind Panagariya. It covers the award period 2026–31; N. K. Singh chaired the 15th FC.

questions.q: Article 163 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Definition of 'the State' for the purposes of Part III
Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor
Promotion of educational and economic interests of SCs, STs and weaker sections
questions.x: Article 163: Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor.

questions.q: The 'Question Hour' in Parliament: a starred question differs from an unstarred question in that it:
o: Requires an oral answer and allows supplementary questions
questions.x: Correct answer: Requires an oral answer and allows supplementary questions. Short-notice questions are asked at less than 10 days' notice.

questions.q: The Constitution (1st Amendment) Act, 1951:
o: Reorganised States on a linguistic basis and abolished Part A, B, C, D classification
Added Sindhi to the Eighth Schedule
Added the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review
Gave effect to the India–Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement (exchange of enclaves)
questions.x: The 1st Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule to protect land reform laws from judicial review.

questions.q: Article 15(6) and Article 16(6), allowing up to 10% reservation for economically weaker sections, were upheld by the Supreme Court in:
o: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022)
questions.x: Correct answer: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022). A five-judge bench upheld the 103rd Amendment by a 3:2 majority.

questions.q: The minimum age for appointment as Governor is:
questions.x: Correct answer: 35 years. Article 157.

questions.q: If a country's exports are $50 billion and imports $70 billion, and net invisibles are +$25 billion, the current account balance is:
questions.x: Correct answer: +$5 billion (surplus). Trade balance −20 + invisibles 25 = +5.

questions.q: Regional Rural Banks were set up in 1975 on the recommendation of the:
questions.x: They are jointly owned by the Centre, the State and a sponsor bank (50:15:35).

questions.q: The 'Green Revolution' in India in the 1960s is most associated with:
o: High-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, irrigation and fertilisers
questions.x: Correct answer: High-yielding varieties of wheat and rice, irrigation and fertilisers. M. S. Swaminathan and Norman Borlaug are key figures.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): India has full capital account convertibility.
Reason (R): FEMA permits free conversion for current account transactions.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is false but R is true. A is false — India has only current account convertibility (with liberalised capital flows). R is true.

questions.q:
In which year did the following happen?
The Foreign Exchange Management Act came into force (replacing FERA).
questions.x: The Foreign Exchange Management Act came into force (replacing FERA) in 2000.

questions.q: The Sagarmala programme focuses on:
questions.x: Correct answer: Port-led development and coastal infrastructure. It aims to reduce logistics costs through modernisation of ports.

questions.q: Budget data (₹ crore): Revenue receipts 32,000; Non-debt capital receipts 4,000; Revenue expenditure 46,000 (of which interest payments 16,000); Capital expenditure 7,000. The revenue deficit is:
questions.x:
Total expenditure = 46,000 + 7,000 = 53,000.
Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure − (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts) = 53,000 − 36,000 = 17,000.
Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit − Interest = 1,000.
Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure − Revenue receipts = 14,000.
Answer (revenue): ₹14,000 crore.

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Revisiting and revitalising the PPP model of infrastructure"?
questions.x: Vijay Kelkar Committee (2015) dealt with revisiting and revitalising the ppp model of infrastructure.

questions.q: According to UN estimates, India became the world's most populous country in:
questions.x: UNFPA's State of World Population report projected India overtaking China in 2023.

questions.q: "Poverty eradication and technological self-reliance" was the focus of which plan?
questions.x: It was the Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980–85).

questions.q: When an auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects are material and pervasive, the auditor issues:
questions.x: Disclaimer arises from pervasive scope limitation; adverse opinion arises from pervasive misstatement.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹45,000; Purchases ₹1,70,000; Purchase returns ₹1,000; Carriage inwards ₹2,000; Sales ₹2,43,500; Sales returns ₹3,000; Closing stock ₹35,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Purchase returns + Carriage inwards − Closing stock
= 45,000 + 1,70,000 − 1,000 + 2,000 − 35,000 = ₹1,81,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 2,43,500 − 3,000 − 1,81,000 = ₹59,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹52,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹1,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹3,500; bank charges debited only in the pass book: ₹400; interest credited only in the pass book: ₹600. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹52,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 1,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 3,500
− Bank charges 400
+ Interest credited 600
Pass book balance = ₹50,200.

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 200 units @ ₹18; 10th — 250 units @ ₹19; 20th — 300 units @ ₹21. 450 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 300 units left come from the latest purchases: 300 × ₹21 = ₹6,300.

questions.q: P and Q share profits in the ratio 5 : 2. They admit R for a 1/4 share, which R acquires from P and Q in their existing ratio. The new profit-sharing ratio of P, Q and R is:

A trader's capital at the beginning of the year was ₹2,05,000 and at the end ₹2,82,500. During the year he introduced fresh capital of ₹25,000 and withdrew ₹17,500 for personal use. His profit for the year is:
questions.x:
Profit = Closing capital + Drawings − Additional capital − Opening capital
= 2,82,500 + 17,500 − 25,000 − 2,05,000 = ₹70,000 (statement of affairs method).

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹1,16,000; selling price ₹245 and variable cost ₹205 per unit. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of ₹80,000?
questions.x:
Required units = (Fixed cost + Target profit) / Contribution per unit
= (1,16,000 + 80,000) / 40 = 4,900 units.

questions.q: Which accounting concept is the basis for charging depreciation over the useful life of an asset rather than writing it off at once?
questions.x: Because the business continues, the asset's cost is allocated to periods benefiting from it.

questions.q: The sales book was undercast by ₹1,000. The rectification entry after preparation of the trial balance (with a suspense account) is:
o: Debtors A/c Dr. To Sales A/c ₹1,000
Sales A/c Dr. To Debtors A/c ₹1,000
Sales A/c Dr. To Suspense A/c ₹1,000
Suspense A/c Dr. To Sales A/c ₹1,000
questions.x: Sales account received ₹1,000 less credit; crediting Sales and debiting Suspense corrects it.

questions.q: Under the Indian Accounting Standards framework, the two fundamental qualitative characteristics of useful financial information are:
questions.x: Comparability, verifiability, timeliness and understandability are enhancing characteristics.

questions.q: Proprietary ratio is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Shareholders' funds ÷ Total assets. It shows the proportion of assets financed by owners.

questions.q: If closing stock is overvalued by ₹5,000 this year, next year's profit will be:
questions.x: This year's closing stock is next year's opening stock; higher opening stock raises next year's COGS.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹30,000, Debtors ₹45,000, Inventory ₹1,00,000, Prepaid expenses ₹2,500, Creditors ₹80,000, Bills payable ₹12,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹10,000. Its quick (acid-test) ratio is:
questions.x:
Quick assets exclude inventory and prepaid expenses: 30,000 + 45,000 = ₹75,000.
Current liabilities = ₹1,02,500.
Quick ratio = 75,000 / 1,02,500 = 0.73 : 1 (benchmark 1 : 1).

questions.q: Ind AS 36 deals with:
questions.x: An asset is impaired when its carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount.

questions.q: Which Act first gave statutory backing to the concept of 'certified standing orders' in India?
questions.x: The 1946 Act required employers to define conditions of employment clearly through certified standing orders.

questions.q: The maximum number of members in a Grievance Redressal Committee under the IR Code is:
questions.x: The committee has equal employer and worker representatives, total not exceeding ten, with chairpersonship alternating annually.

questions.q: Regularisation of temporary or ad hoc government employees cannot be claimed as a matter of right, held the Constitution Bench in:
o: Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadevi (2006)
questions.x: Umadevi (2006) held that public employment must follow constitutional recruitment; irregular appointees cannot claim regularisation.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, the Central Government is the 'appropriate government' for all of the following EXCEPT:
o: A private textile mill in Coimbatore
questions.x: The Centre is the appropriate government for railways, mines, oil fields, major ports, air transport, banking, insurance and Central PSUs; a private textile mill is under the State Government.

questions.q: In Dunlop's model, the output of an industrial relations system is:
o: A web of rules governing the workplace
questions.x: The system produces a 'web of rules' — procedural and substantive rules that govern employment relations.

questions.q: 'Moonlighting' in employment refers to:
o: Working overtime in the same firm
Holding a second job alongside one's primary employment
questions.x: Correct answer: Holding a second job alongside one's primary employment. Moonlighting became widely debated in India's IT sector in 2022.

questions.q: For an Indian employee posted abroad by an Indian employer to a country with which India has an SSA, the document certifying continued coverage under Indian social security is the:
o: Certificate of Coverage (CoC) issued by EPFO
No Objection Certificate from the MEA
questions.x: EPFO issues a Certificate of Coverage so that the detached worker is exempt from contributing in the host country.

questions.q: Lay-off compensation under the IR Code is payable at what rate of basic wages plus dearness allowance?
questions.x: A laid-off worker gets compensation equal to 50% of basic wages and DA for the days of lay-off (other than weekly holidays).

questions.q: Under the Labour Codes, the designation 'Inspector-cum-Facilitator' signals a shift towards:
o: Inspections only on written complaint by a trade union
Transfer of inspection powers to industry associations
Advising employers on compliance besides inspecting, with randomised web-based inspection schemes
questions.x: The Codes rename inspectors as Inspector-cum-Facilitators who also guide compliance; inspection schemes may be web-based and randomised to reduce discretion.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, if a worker is laid off for more than 45 days in a 12-month period (in an establishment below the Chapter X threshold), the employer may:
o: Transfer the worker to another company
Retrench the worker after paying retrenchment compensation, with lay-off compensation adjusted
questions.x: After 45 days of lay-off, the employer may retrench the worker by following retrenchment conditions; lay-off compensation already paid may be set off.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'wages' as defined in the Code on Wages:
1. House rent allowance is excluded from wages.
2. Dearness allowance is included in wages.
3. Statutory bonus forms part of wages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is incorrect.
Wages include basic pay, DA and retaining allowance. HRA, statutory bonus, overtime, commission, conveyance and gratuity are excluded (subject to the 50% rule).

questions.q: A contract worker claims to be absorbed by the principal employer after contract labour in the process is prohibited. As per SAIL v. National Union Waterfront Workers (2001), the worker:
o: Has no automatic right of absorption, but may be given preference in regular recruitment
questions.x: The Constitution Bench held there is no automatic absorption; the principal employer should give preference to the erstwhile contract workers if it employs regular workers.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Directive Principles such as the living wage are not enforceable by courts.
Reason (R): Article 37 states that the Directive Principles are fundamental in governance but not enforceable by any court.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Article 37 makes DPSPs non-justiciable, though courts use them to interpret laws such as those on wages and social security.

questions.q: The National Child Labour Project (NCLP), started in 1988, was aimed at:
o: Training children as apprentices in factories
Rescuing child workers and mainstreaming them through special training centres
questions.x: NCLP ran special training centres for rescued children; it has since been merged with Samagra Shiksha (2021).

questions.q: In Municipal Corporation of Delhi v. Female Workers (Muster Roll) (2000), the Supreme Court held that:
o: Maternity benefit applies only to permanent employees
Women engaged on muster roll (daily wage) are entitled to maternity benefit
Female workers cannot be engaged on daily wages
questions.x: The Court extended maternity benefit to casual/muster-roll women workers, citing Article 42 and CEDAW.

questions.q: Which of the following is among the laws consolidated in the OSH Code?
o: Cine-Workers and Cinema Theatre Workers (Regulation of Employment) Act, 1981
questions.x: The Cine-Workers and Cinema Theatre Workers (RoE) Act went into the OSH Code; the Cine-Workers Welfare Fund Act went into the Code on Social Security.

questions.q: For updating the date of birth in EPF records, EPFO accepts which of the following as primary proof?
questions.x: Documents such as birth certificates or school certificates are primary proofs; Aadhaar is accepted within limits as per EPFO circulars.

questions.q: Extended sickness benefit under ESI for long-term diseases is payable at what rate and for how long?
o: 80% of wages, up to two years, for 34 notified diseases
questions.x: Extended sickness benefit covers notified long-term diseases such as cancer and TB, at 80% up to two years.

questions.q: The Government's contribution under the Unified Pension Scheme is:
questions.x: The Government contributes 18.5% (employee 10%) to fund the assured payout.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): An EPF account becomes 'inoperative' when there is no contribution for 36 months after the member retires after 55, emigrates or dies.
Reason (R): Interest is not credited to inoperative accounts.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true, but R does not explain A. Both statements are correct as per the EPF Scheme rules (2016 amendment), but R is a consequence of inoperative status rather than the reason why accounts become inoperative.

questions.q: Under the maternity benefit law, after availing maternity benefit, a woman may be allowed to work from home if:
o: The nature of work permits and on terms mutually agreed with the employer
The employer is a government department
questions.x: The 2017 amendment enables work from home where the work permits, on mutually agreed terms.

questions.q: The power to notify an industry or class of establishments for EPF coverage (Schedule I) rests with:
questions.x: The Central Government may add industries to Schedule I or notify classes of establishments.

questions.q: Under the Code on Social Security, the Central Government may frame schemes for gig and platform workers covering:
o: Life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old-age protection and creche
questions.x: Correct answer: Life and disability cover, accident insurance, health and maternity benefits, old-age protection and creche. Section 114 lists the areas for schemes for gig and platform workers.

questions.q: An employee draws basic wages plus DA of ₹35,500 per month and both employer and employee contribute 12% on actual wages. How much of the employer's share goes to the EPF (provident fund) account each month?
questions.x:
Employer's 12% of 35,500 = ₹4,260.
EPS share is capped at 8.33% of ₹15,000 = ₹1,250.
EPF share = 4,260 − 1,250 = ₹3,010.

questions.q: The difference between 'social insurance' and 'social assistance' is that social assistance is generally:
o: Financed by employer and employee contributions
Available only to the organised sector
questions.x: Social insurance (EPF, ESI) is contributory; social assistance (NSAP pensions) is non-contributory and needs-based.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹11,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 10%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,500) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(11,500, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 10% = ₹8,400. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): EPS 1995 provides a minimum pension of ₹1,000 per month.
Reason (R): Every EPS member contributes 1.16% of wages to fund the minimum pension.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true but R is false. A is true. R is false — the 1.16% is contributed by the Central Government, which also gives budgetary support for the minimum pension.

questions.q: The age group for enrolment in PMJJBY is:
questions.x: Subscribers can join between 18 and 50, with cover continuing till 55 on payment of premium.

questions.q: A galvanometer is used to measure:
questions.x: Galvanometer: Small electric currents.

questions.q: 'Quantum computing' uses:
o: Qubits that can exist in superposition of states
questions.x: Correct answer: Qubits that can exist in superposition of states. It can solve certain problems much faster than classical computers.

questions.q: An operating system is:
o: System software that manages hardware and provides services to application programs
questions.x: Correct answer: System software that manages hardware and provides services to application programs. Examples: Windows, Linux, macOS, Android.

questions.q: Malicious software that encrypts a victim's files and demands payment is called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Ransomware. Backups and patching help prevent damage.

questions.q: NavIC is India's:
questions.x: Correct answer: Regional satellite navigation system. It provides positioning services over India and surrounding regions.

questions.q: In computing, 'SaaS' stands for:
questions.x: SaaS = Software as a Service.

questions.q: Cooking takes longer at high altitudes because:
o: Water boils at a lower temperature due to lower air pressure
questions.x: Correct answer: Water boils at a lower temperature due to lower air pressure. Food cooks at a lower temperature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sound travels faster in solids than in air.
2. Light needs a medium to travel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
Light can travel through vacuum.

questions.q: Which is the main constituent of natural gas and biogas?
questions.x: Biogas contains about 50–75% methane.

questions.q: A 100 W bulb used for 5 hours a day for 30 days consumes:
questions.x: Correct answer: 15 units (kWh). 100 W × 5 h × 30 = 15,000 Wh = 15 kWh.

questions.q: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Stapes (in the middle ear). The femur (thigh bone) is the longest.

questions.q: Type 1 diabetes is mainly due to:
o: Lack of insulin production by the pancreas
questions.x: Correct answer: Lack of insulin production by the pancreas. Type 2 diabetes involves insulin resistance.

questions.q: A motor boat goes 24 km downstream in 2 hours and returns the same distance upstream in 6 hours. The speed of the stream is:
questions.x:
Downstream speed = 24/2 = 12 km/h; upstream speed = 24/6 = 4 km/h.
Stream = (down − up)/2 = (12 − 4)/2 = 4 km/h (boat in still water = 8 km/h).

questions.q: The monthly incomes of P and Q are in the ratio 5 : 6 and their monthly expenditures are in the ratio 3 : 7. If each of them saves ₹21,250 a month, P's monthly income is:
questions.x:
Let incomes = 5k, 6k and expenditures = 3m, 7m.
5k − 3m = 6k − 7m = 21,250 → -1k = -4m.
Solving gives k = 5,000, m = 1,250.
P's income = 5 × 5,000 = ₹25,000 (check: ₹25,000 − ₹3,750 = ₹21,250).

questions.q: A bag has 7 white and 11 black balls. Two balls are drawn at random together. What is the probability that at least one of them is white?
questions.x:
P(at least one white) = 1 − P(both black).
P(both black) = C(11,2)/C(18,2) = 55/153.
Required = 1 − 55/153 = 98/153.

questions.q: The average age of 33 trainees in a batch is 10 years. When the instructor's age is also included, the average rises by 1 year. The instructor's age is:
questions.x:
Total of trainees = 33 × 10 = 330.
With instructor: 34 × 11 = 374.
Instructor = 374 − 330 = 44 years.

questions.q: At what time between 1 and 2 o'clock will the hands of a clock point in opposite directions (be in a straight line but opposite)?
questions.x:
At 1:00 the minute hand is 5 minute-spaces behind the hour hand.
To be opposite it must gain 5 + 30 = 35 spaces; it gains 55 spaces in 60 minutes.
Time = 35 × 60/55 = 420/11 minutes = 38 2/11 minutes past 1.

questions.q: The ratio of the present ages of P and Q is 9 : 7. After 8 years, the ratio will become 31 : 25. What is P's present age?
The number of claims settled by a regional office rises by 10%, then falls by 20%, and finally rises by 10%. The overall percentage change is:
questions.x:
Multiply the growth factors: (1 + 10/100) × (1 − 20/100) × (1 + 10/100) = 1.1 × 0.8 × 1.1 = 0.968.
Overall change = (0.968 − 1) × 100 = -3.2% → 3.2% decrease.
Note: simply adding (10 − 20 + 10) is wrong because each change acts on a new base.

questions.q: Find the greatest number that will divide 644, 860, 1364 leaving the same remainder in each case.
questions.x:
If N leaves the same remainder, N divides the differences.
Differences: 860 − 644 = 216, 1364 − 860 = 504.
HCF(216, 504) = 72.

questions.q: ₹14,000 is invested for 1 year at 20% per annum, interest being compounded half-yearly. The compound interest earned is:
questions.x:
Half-yearly: rate per period = 20/2 = 10%, number of periods = 2.
Amount = 14,000 × (1 + 10/100)² = ₹16,940.
CI = ₹2,940 (slightly more than annual compounding, which gives ₹2,800).

questions.q: The marks of students are: 35, 78, 48, 62, 59, 91, 18. Their arithmetic mean is:
questions.x: Sum = 391; number of values = 7. Mean = 391/7 = 55.86.

questions.q: How many arrangements of the letters of 'BENEFIT' are there in which the vowels are NOT all together?
questions.x:
Total arrangements = 2,520 (E appears 2 times).
Vowels together = 120 × 3 = 360.
Not all together = 2,520 − 360 = 2,160.

questions.q:
Production of a fertiliser unit (thousand tonnes) — 2021: 285  |  2022: 255  |  2023: 300  |  2024: 325  |  2025: 300.
In which year was the percentage growth over the previous year the highest?
questions.x:
Year-on-year growth: 2022: -10.53%; 2023: 17.65%; 2024: 8.33%; 2025: -7.69%.
Highest growth: 2023 (17.65%). Note: the largest absolute rise need not be the largest percentage rise.

questions.q: In a certain code language, QUOTA is written as EXSYU. How is MEMBER written in that code?
questions.x:
Compare QUOTA → EXSYU: Q→U, U→Y, O→S…
Rule: the word is written in reverse order and then each letter is moved 4 places forward.
Applying it to MEMBER gives VIFQIQ.

questions.q: A vessel holds 60 litres of pure milk. 12 litres are drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is repeated once more. How much milk is now in the vessel?
questions.x:
After n replacements, milk = x(1 − y/x)ⁿ.
= 60 × (1 − 12/60)² = 60 × (0.8)² = 38.4 litres.
Removing 2 × 12 directly is wrong because the second draw removes a mixture, not pure milk.
